extracted.intended_audience: general readers of English-language China/business news
extracted.subtask_description: A news report of a controversial commercial and the public and corporate responses, illustrating the criteria by which an ad and its apology are judged (e.g., sexism, cultural sensitivity, sincerity, retraction, corporate oversight). Useful for assessing ad offensiveness and appropriate corporate remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sexist or demeaning content
rubrics_metrics.description: The ad was widely criticized for 'likening women to used cars' and for being 'sexist and demeaning to females.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not craft creative content that compares people to objects or otherwise dehumanizes a group; netizen comments show such comparisons provoke strong backlash (e.g., 'Such a vulgar ad! Likening women to used cars?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough consideration in creativity and details
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi stated: 'It is the lacking of thorough consideration in creativity and details that led to the content (of the ad) making the public hold the opinion it is sexist and demeaning to females.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vetting creative concepts and execution carefully before release can prevent unintended offensive readings; review both high-level idea and specific visual/physical actions portrayed (e.g., pinching, gazing at body parts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue a sincere public apology and accept criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi 'sincerely accepts the criticism and suggestions of the public' and 'deeply regrets' the ad, issuing apologies on WeChat and to USA Today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective response should acknowledge harm, accept criticism, express regret, and communicate corrective steps. Note: public skepticism can remain if apology is perceived as insincere ('This is not an apology, but a surrender to money').

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate retraction of offensive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi 'announced an immediate retraction of the advertisement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawing the ad promptly limits further harm and distribution; retraction is expected as part of remediation when an ad causes public offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider target market and local cultural norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi noted the ad was 'targeted only to the Chinese market'; netizens said the commercial distorted Chinese marriage and the mother-in-law/daughter-in-law relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt messaging to local cultural sensitivities and avoid misrepresenting or caricaturing culturally specific relationships; what might be acceptable in one market can be offensive in another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vulgarity and misalignment with brand values
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters called the commercial 'vulgar' and questioned whether it reflects what Audi stands for ('Is this what Audi is all about? So low!').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure creative approaches fit the luxury/brand positioning and do not rely on crude or sensational depictions that can damage brand reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discriminate or shame people who had plastic surgery
rubrics_metrics.description: Netizens criticized the commercial for 'Discrimination against people who received plastic surgery.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid messaging that mocks or marginalizes individuals based on appearance choices or medical/cosmetic procedures; such content can be perceived as discriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear explanation, accountability and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Netizens complained that 'no one from such a big company can explain the problem of this commercial' and did not accept the apology as adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond an apology, companies should offer explanations of how the mistake occurred, who was responsible, and what concrete steps will be taken to prevent recurrence; perceived evasiveness fuels distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure corporate oversight across divisions / joint ventures
rubrics_metrics.description: Audi noted the ad was 'conceived by the used cars division of its joint venture in China.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent companies and central brand teams must oversee creative approvals across all divisions and partners to prevent locally produced content from harming the wider brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor social media/public reaction and engage appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The article lists multiple social media reactions on Weibo and notes continued skepticism despite the apology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively monitor online discourse to gauge sentiment and respond promptly; engagement should aim to address concerns substantively rather than merely performative statements.
